CHIEF COMPLAINT
Numbness and tingling in bilateral hands

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
60-year-old right-handed male referred for evaluation of numbness and tingling in bilateral hands. Symptoms began several weeks ago following a motor vehicle accident in December with bilateral wrist fractures. On the right side, symptoms extend from the middle and ring fingers up the forearm. On the left side, symptoms extend from the pinky and ring fingers. Patient reports soreness, occasional throbbing, and weakness, particularly with use. Tingling is more pronounced when painful but becomes dull when pain resolves. Symptoms are worse at night and fluctuate throughout the day. Denies loss of sensation but notes decreased sensitivity. Patient also reports mild neck stiffness since hitting his head during the accident (noted as contusion at that time). Wears splints on both wrists, right worse than left, which provide some relief. Symptoms have worsened significantly over the past month. Patient has not been compliant with prescribed nerve pain medication.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Constitutional: Fatigue and weight gain. GI: Excessive appetite and bloating. Eyes: Floaters. Cardiovascular: Shortness of breath and leg swelling. Endocrine: Polyphagia. Skin: Nail bed changes, dryness, and itching. Musculoskeletal: Gout and muscle pain. Remainder of review of systems negative.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Bilateral wrist fractures from motor vehicle accident (December, healed)
Head contusion from motor vehicle accident (December)
Prediabetes (controlled with diet modification)
Hypertension
Anxiety disorder

MEDICATIONS
Coreg (for hypertension)
Lexapro (for anxiety)
Nerve pain medication (prescribed but not compliant with dosing)

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Right-handed. Recent motor vehicle accident with significant trauma.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Neurologic exam: Sensation normal except pin prick sensation diminished in third and fourth fingers on right and decreased in fourth and fifth fingers on left. Reflexes 1+ and symmetric in upper extremities; 2+ in knees; toes downgoing bilaterally. Tinel sign positive at both wrists and both elbows. Rest of exam normal.

RESULTS
Pending: EMG study to localize nerve irritation and determine site of compression.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome, likely secondary to trauma from motor vehicle accident with bilateral wrist fractures. EMG study ordered to precisely localize nerve irritation and confirm diagnosis. Continue wearing bilateral wrist splints. Patient to return for follow-up visit after EMG results. If symptoms persist, referral to hand clinic for possible injections or carpal tunnel release surgery, or referral to orthopedics for same intervention will be considered.
